Regional news roundup for the first week of March. The city council approved a new budget for road repairs after a long debate. A strong M6.1 earthquake struck off the coast of Honshu on March 3, 2026, according to the national survey. The quake was felt widely across the region and shaking lasted about a minute. No tsunami warning was issued, officials said. Aftershocks continued through the following day, the largest of magnitude 4.8. Schools reopened on March 5 after inspections found no structural damage. In sports, the local team won its third game in a row. The weather stayed mild for most of the week, with light rain on Thursday. A new bakery opened on the main street and drew long lines on its first morning. The museum extended its hours for the spring exhibit. Volunteers planted trees along the river path on Saturday. The library will host a talk about earthquake preparedness next month, with tips for households and small businesses.
